title: Material, work, care, and health conditions do not automatically become trust or political action
source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled cross-source architecture using SIPP person-month transitions, ATUS diary-day contrasts, MEPS longitudinal persons, ANES panel respondents, and CCES respondents

observations.period: 2024 reference year; SIPP resource-to-work transition by work-limiting status

denominator.unit: identified SIPP persons; valid adjacent-pair universes vary by measure

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month SIPP cross-lag using resource band, work-limiting status, hours, earnings, and Fay-BRR replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: The result is a descriptive work/resource stage; change has no inferred direction and does not measure attribution, trust, care response, or political action.
observations.subgroup: Reported work-limiting condition versus no reported condition, stratified by resource band.
observations.counterinterpretation: Composition, reporting, opportunity, hours preference, earnings level, and job mix can explain the contrast.

denominator.unit: ATUS respondents in supported standardization cells; provider n=1,315

eldercare_difference_minutes.unit: provider minus nonprovider minutes per diary day; SE 7.134

observations.method: ATUS diary aggregation with eldercare-roster provider status and replicate-weight standardization across supported demographic, labor-force, child, and education cells.
observations.uncertainty: Annual diary respondents are not a panel; the contrast does not identify care onset, recipient outcome, employer response, health, or a political interpretation.
observations.subgroup: Eldercare providers versus nonproviders within supported standardization cells.
observations.counterinterpretation: Provider selection, recipient need, distance, household support, and employment choice can generate the time contrast; less work time is not automatically work loss.

denominator.unit: MEPS Panel 27 persons with positive longitudinal weight and valid paired fields

out_of_pocket_expenditure_change.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

employed_both_endpoint_rounds.unit: percent of valid persons; separate employment-status universe
employed_both_endpoint_rounds.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

employed_to_not_employed.unit: percent of valid persons; separate employment-status universe
employed_to_not_employed.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

not_employed_to_employed.unit: percent of valid persons; separate employment-status universe
not_employed_to_employed.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

wage_income_change.unit: 2023 minus 2022 dollars per person; separate valid paired wage universe
wage_income_change.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

observations.method: MEPS Panel 27 five-round longitudinal person analysis with positive longitudinal weights and paired health-status and expenditure fields.
observations.uncertainty: Health-cost co-movement is not evidence that work limitation or care time caused the change, and expenditure is not a complete household budget measure.
observations.subgroup: MEPS longitudinal persons with valid paired fields; income-stratified results remain in the source record.
observations.counterinterpretation: Total spending can rise while out-of-pocket spending falls, and health can improve or worsen without identifying a time, work, or care mechanism.

observations.period: 2024 pre-election to post-election; ANES panel financial worry, trust, and reported vote

denominator.unit: valid weighted panel observations for trust cross-tab; vote cross-tab uses 1,699

observations.method: Official ANES 2024 Full Release SDA weighted descriptive cross-tabs in the retained 2016-2020-2024 panel subset.
observations.uncertainty: Financial worry is not a dated material event; party identity, prior beliefs, information, panel retention, and retrospective judgment remain alternative explanations. No causal contrast is reproduced.
observations.subgroup: Financial-worry rows, with trust and reported presidential vote outcomes; party-conditioned patterns are retained in the related finding.
observations.counterinterpretation: A worry/trust or worry/vote pattern can reflect identity and joint interpretation rather than material pressure producing political action.

observations.period: 2024 post-election; CCES material proxies, institutional trust, and civic action

denominator.unit: valid respondents in the no-gig/no-student-loan reference cell; other joint cells are separately denominated

observations.method: Weighted CCES common-post respondent comparison using commonpostweight; trust and any-action fields are coded as defined in the source record.
observations.uncertainty: Cross-sectional material proxies do not establish event timing, attribution, prior trust, remedy, or causality; complex-survey variance was not reproduced in this pass.
observations.subgroup: Joint gig-work and current student-loan-responsibility proxy cells.
observations.counterinterpretation: Age, education, income, employment selection, party identity, and other composition can explain joint trust/action differences.

related_sources.claim: SIPP, ATUS, and MEPS supply the material, work, care, and health stages without a common respondent join.
ANES supplies a panel-level worry/trust/reported-vote stage with identity and causal boundaries.
CCES supplies joint material-proxy, institutional-trust, and civic-action comparisons.

boundary: This is a non-pooled architecture record, not a causal pathway estimate. It shows that the program now has evidence surfaces for material/work/care/health, trust, and civic or political action, while the same-person dated trigger-to-attribution-to-action link remains open. The currencies, populations, denominators, dates, and estimands must not be collapsed into a burden index or a vote mechanism.
